rollouts.answer: The item mapped to RT + left on the D-pad is 聚命丹 (around 79,367s).

rollouts.answer: The item mapped to RT + left is 'Red Tides'.
rollouts.tool_call_sequence: read_skill x4 -> semantic_search x3 -> run_sql x2 -> clip_qa(79050-79110) -> submit

decisive_steps.what_happened: run_sql over episodes 79000-79500 correctly located the Bu Yunlu fight window, but the agent then issued a single narrow clip_qa call for 79050-79110s, i.e. right up to (and not past) the start of the clue interval, before the item wheel with legible Chinese text ever appears on screen (that only shows up around t=79360-79420 in the other rollouts).

clip_qa's evidence frames at t~79057-79070s show an early RT item wheel with unlabeled icons only (no visible text at all, pre-fight loadout). With no legible text present, the sub-agent still returned a specific English name 'Red Tides' that appears nowhere in the frame, i.e. a fabricated answer rather than an 'unreadable' report.

rollouts.failure_point: Time window chosen for clip_qa stopped at the very start of the clue interval and never reached the later in-fight frames where the item label becomes legible; combined with the sub-agent hallucinating a plausible-sounding but fabricated English name instead of flagging illegible/no-text icons.
rollouts.evidence_checked: copy-frame of both evidence_frame_ids at t=79057-79070s: icons visible but no readable text in the crop; 'Red Tides' does not correspond to anything on screen and is not a real item name pattern used elsewhere in this game's HUD (all real items in this fight are Chinese-labeled, e.g. 保命丹, 龙光倍力丸, 如意画轴, 缩地青符).

db_evidence.notes: SQL search over entities and semantic_triples for '%命丹%' / '%Life%' returned zero rows: the structured memory DB (episodes/entities/semantic_triples/topic_facts) never captured the on-screen HUD item-wheel text at all — it is not OCR'd or entity-extracted anywhere in the timeline's memory tables. The fact is only recoverable by calling clip_qa on the source video and visually reading the radial-wheel HUD, which is legible (left slot = 保命丹, clearly readable) at multiple points during the fight (confirmed at t=79367.011s and t=79420.011s), well after the tight 79110-79114s clue_interval which just marks the start of the encounter.

root_causes: The item-wheel HUD text is entirely absent from the structured memory DB (episodes/entities/semantic_triples all return zero hits for the item name), so every rollout's success or failure hinges purely on clip_qa's visual OCR/reading of small on-screen Chinese text.

clip_qa is unreliable at reading small in-game HUD text even when the correct frame is retrieved: rollout 0 read 保命丹 as 聚命丹 (one-character error, still scored 5) and rollout 2 read the same legible label as an unrelated item 聚气丹 (scored 0) from an equally legible frame.

The game exposes two visually similar radial wheels near the same time window: an item wheel (D-pad + RT, labels like 保命丹/龙光倍力丸/如意画轴/缩地青符) and a skill wheel (face buttons X/Y/A/B, labels like 定身法/铜头铁臂/金蟬/身外身法). Rollout 3's clip_qa answered from the wrong wheel (the skill wheel) without noticing the button-glyph mismatch.

Rollout 4 anchored its clip_qa window too early (79050-79110s, ending exactly at the clue_interval start) and never reached the later part of the fight (around 79360-79420s) where the item wheel actually becomes legible with text; with no legible text in its sampled frames, the sub-agent fabricated a plausible-sounding but nonexistent English item name ('Red Tides') instead of reporting the icons were unreadable.

The judge appears to grade on gloss/semantic closeness to the English reference 'Life-Saving Pill' rather than exact Chinese-string match: a one-character misread ('聚命丹' vs correct '保命丹') still scored 5, while a wholly different item name ('聚气丹') scored 0.
what_worked: Rollouts 0 and 1 both chose (or arrived at) clip_qa windows extending well past the clue_interval into the mid/late fight (79110-79440s and 79320-79440s respectively), which is where the item radial wheel with legible text actually appears on screen.

Correctly narrowing the SQL/semantic search to the Bu Yunlu fight's episode time range (~79000-79500s) before invoking clip_qa, done by all 5 rollouts, successfully located the right general window even when the final clip_qa sub-window choice later failed.
transferable_lessons: For questions about on-screen HUD/controller-mapping text, do not expect the structured memory DB to help — go straight to clip_qa, and query it over a window that extends well past the start of the clue_interval, since the labelled UI element may only become legible several minutes into the event.

When a game/video has multiple visually similar HUD radial menus, explicitly instruct clip_qa to identify which control scheme triggers the wheel (e.g. 'the wheel opened by holding RT and pressing D-pad directions, NOT the face-button X/Y/A/B skill wheel') so the sub-agent doesn't answer from the wrong one.

Treat a single clip_qa text-read as unverified: when the on-screen text is small, cross-check by sampling a second independent frame/time before submitting, since the same legible label was read correctly by some rollouts and misread or hallucinated by others.

A visual sub-agent should report 'icons visible but no legible text' rather than inventing a specific-sounding but fabricated name when the sampled frames genuinely lack readable text (as happened in rollout 4).
open_questions: Whether clip_qa's own frame-sampling resolution/downscaling (as opposed to prompt wording) is the primary driver of the read errors in rollouts 0 and 2, given the same underlying source frame was legible enough for a human/analyst to read directly.

Whether the judge's grading criterion is a fixed semantic-similarity threshold to the English reference, which would explain scoring the one-character misread '聚命丹' as full credit (5) while a differently-named item '聚气丹' scored 0.
